offence_severity: Imprisonment which may extend to ten years, and also liable to fine
number_of_offences: Five offences charged, four finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the 'suicide note' written by the deceased Sushila as key evidence, which indicated that she had left her residence by her own free will and committed suicide.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses, including the deceased's family, and found that the prosecution failed to produce any other evidence to demonstrate that the appellant had enticed the deceased or forced her into any act.
bail_history: Appellant was enlarged on bail by the Court's motion Bench order dated 15.04.2011. His bail bonds shall stand discharged.
trial_duration: Trial judgment: 05.01.2011; High Court decision: 05.01.2011; Supreme Court decision: 09.12.2015
legal_representation: For the Appellant: G. Chaudhary, Sr.Adv., Suresh C. Gupta, Birendra K. Mishra, Ms. Poonam Atey; For the Respondents: Deepak Thukral, Dy. AG., Arun Tewatia, Asstt. AG, R. C. Kaushik
appeal_history: Trial court: Acquittal of uncle and aunt; conviction of appellant; High Court: Upheld the order of conviction; Supreme Court: Allowed the appeal and set aside the conviction
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant kidnapped a minor girl and raped her, with his uncle and aunt helping to conceal her, leading to her murder by administering poison.
defence_argument: The defence relied on the 'suicide note' written by the deceased, stating that she had left her residence by her own free will and committed suicide, not being forced or compelled to marry the appellant.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that the prosecution must establish the guilt of the accused beyond a reasonable doubt, and that the suicide note provided a clear and unequivocal statement of the deceased's intent.
